evaluations.rationale: Fields to enter (name, optional description) are concrete and not open to materially different interpretations.
Inviting by providing a URL is clear and unambiguous about how invitation occurs.
Describes a concrete action (entering an item in a multi-line text field) with little room for multiple interpretations.
Seeing all items for the session is a straightforward concept; terms are sufficiently specific in context.
Selecting an item to be estimated/re-estimated is concrete and not open to materially different interpretations.
Adding an item to the list is a concrete action; intent ('be flexible') is not a source of requirement ambiguity.

Editing an item to reflect team understanding is a common, sufficiently clear request; although 'better reflect' is subjective, it does not create materially different requirement interpretations at story level.
Deleting an item so it is not estimated is clear and not open to multiple material interpretations.
Showing all estimates immediately (even if some estimators haven't given estimates) is explicit about behavior and not materially ambiguous.
The term 'average' is ambiguous (mean, median, mode, trimmed mean etc.) and can lead to materially different implementations.
Automatically filling the estimate when all show the same card is specific and not open to multiple interpretations.
Entering an agreed-upon estimate is clear; the artifact and intent are unambiguous for implementation.
Re-estimating a previously estimated story is concrete and not open to materially different interpretations.
Importing stories from a spreadsheet is a clear user intent; specific format details belong to acceptance criteria but the story itself is unambiguous.
Copy/paste from a spreadsheet is a concrete action; wording is not materially ambiguous.
Browsing previous games to find one is a clear requirement and not open to multiple material interpretations.
Viewing a transcript to see stories and estimates is specific and unambiguous in intent.
Exporting a transcript as an HTML file is explicit and not ambiguous.
Export as CSV for further processing is a concrete format request and unambiguous.
Deleting a game so its stories and estimates are no longer stored is clear in intent and effect.
Account creation with specific fields (name, email, password, username) is concrete and unambiguous.
Logging in with account name and password is a standard, clear requirement.
Changing account details is a common, understandable story; although fields are unspecified, the core intent is not ambiguous.
Deleting an account to remove stored account information and games is explicit and unambiguous in outcome.
Showing dates/times in the user's local timezone is a clear requirement; implementation details can be specified later without semantic ambiguity.
Receiving a password reminder by email is concrete and not open to materially different interpretations.
Specifies two concrete card sets (modified Fibonacci or powers of two), which is precise and unambiguous.
'Invite up to 15 estimators' is a precise numeric limit and not ambiguous.
Joining by entering a name on the provided URL page is concrete and clear.
Seeing the item being estimated is a clear, specific requirement.
Viewing all items planned for the session is straightforward and not ambiguous.
Seeing immediately who has given an estimate is explicit and implementation-independent but not ambiguous semantically.
Showing all estimates at the same time after all have been given is explicit and not open to multiple material interpretations.
Allowing estimate changes until the last person selects a card is specific about the condition and not ambiguous.
'Each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated' is a sufficiently specific notion (prior estimates for this story) and not materially ambiguous.
Seeing who gave what during the current round is concrete and clear.
Starting a two-minute countdown visible to all participants is an explicit, unambiguous requirement.
Resetting the two-minute timer when all play an estimate is explicit about the trigger and outcome and not ambiguous.
Scrolling back through prior rounds' stories and estimates is concrete and understandable.
Having cards in the same order across draws is specific and not open to materially different interpretations.
Changing an estimate while the draw is incomplete is a clear condition and unambiguous.
Displaying a small thumbnail near played cards is a concrete UI requirement and not materially ambiguous.
Stating compliance with 'XHTML and CSS standards' without specifying versions/levels or conformance criteria can be interpreted materially differently (which validators/levels to meet).
A list of definitions for commonly used terms is a clear deliverable and not ambiguous in intent.
The phrase 'as fast as possible' is vague and can lead to materially different performance expectations and implementations.
Specifying exact browser versions for correct function is concrete and unambiguous.
The qualifier 'where possible' makes compliance with W3C accessibility guidelines ambiguous and can be interpreted variably as to what is required.
The term 'respond quickly' lacks measurable criteria (latency thresholds) and can be implemented in materially different ways.
Supporting Unicode so users can use any language is a clear technical requirement and not open to materially different interpretations at story level.
Terms like 'sensible' and 'predictable' are subjective and can lead to materially different expectations for URL structure.
Describing error pages as 'nice' is subjective and underspecified, allowing diverse interpretations of what is required.
Storing results in a 'non-identifiable way' is ambiguous without specifying anonymization techniques or acceptable re-identification risk, leading to materially different implementations.
Requesting 'some metrics' is underspecified (which metrics, granularity, time windows) and can be interpreted in many materially different ways.
